The `abort()` is unreachable: `fread(buf, 1, sizeof(buf), f)` caps `n` at 64, so `n > 999` can never be true. Let me run an exhaustive probe matrix to confirm no edge case (FIFO, directory, missing file, huge file) behaves differently between the two binaries.<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "cd /tmp && rm -rf probe && mkdir probe && cd probe
cc -O0 -o vuln ~/vuln.c 2>/dev/null || cc -O0 -o vuln "$OLDPWD/vuln.c"
cc -O0 -o fixed "$OLDPWD/fixed.c"
VDIR="$OLDPWD"
: > empty.bin
head -c 64 /dev/urandom > b64.bin
head -c 65 /dev/urandom > b65.bin
head -c 1000 /dev/urandom > b1000.bin
head -c 1048576 /dev/zero > b1m.bin
mkfifo pipe.fifo 2>/dev/null
( head -c 100 /dev/urandom > pipe.fifo & ) 2>/dev/null
for f in empty.bin b64.bin b65.bin b1000.bin b1m.bin pipe.fifo nonexistent missing_dir; do
  ./vuln "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; V=$?
  ./fixed "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; F=$?
  echo "$f -> vuln=$V fixed=$F"
done
./vuln >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "noarg -> vuln=$?"
./fixed >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "noarg -> fixed=$?"
echo '--- direct check that n can never exceed 64:'
cat > t.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(){char b[64];FILE*f=fopen("b1m.bin","rb");size_t n=fread(b,1,sizeof(b),f);printf("n=%zu\n",n);return 0;}
EOF
cc -O0 -o t t.c && ./t"}}
</action>
